sources.title: Official Gemma 4 12B IT model card
sources.evidence: The exact IT repository identifies the Gemma 4 12B Unified variant, Apache 2.0 open weights, text/image/audio/video input and text output. Its dense-model table labels total parameters 11.95B, 48 layers and 256K context. It documents configurable thinking and function calling. Freshly reopened the pinned raw README on October 27: its metadata explicitly names google/gemma-4-12B as the base model; the separate active-parameter row is 3.8B for 26B A4B only, not the dense 12B column.

sources.title: Gemma releases
sources.evidence: Explicitly records the release of Gemma 4 12B Unified on June 3, 2026. The June 9 baseline date is later than the documented public release.

sources.title: Gemma 4 12B: The Developer Guide
sources.evidence: Dated June 3, 2026. Describes a dense decoder-only Transformer with a 35M vision embedder, direct audio waveform projection and a separate dedicated MTP draft model.

sources.title: Official 12B IT checkpoint configuration
sources.evidence: Ungated config identifies Gemma4UnifiedForConditionalGeneration; 48 layers, hidden size 3840, 40 sliding and 8 full-attention layers, no MoE, max_position_embeddings 262144, vocabulary 262144 and tied word embeddings. Audio and vision projection configurations are present.

sources.title: Official 12B IT safetensors header
sources.evidence: Read only HTTP 206 ranges 0-7 and 8-88959, not tensor payloads. The 677 tensor entries contain 11,959,730,224 BF16 stored elements, including 48 one-element layer_scalar entries. Applying Transformers nn.Parameter versus nn.Buffer classification yields 11,959,730,176 parameter elements; scalar training provenance remains unresolved. Both counts round to 11.9597B. All multimodal components are present; no separate MTP or duplicate lm_head tensors are present.

sources.title: Transformers Gemma 4 Unified implementation
sources.evidence: Defines layer_scalar as nn.Buffer and ties lm_head.weight to model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight. RoPE frequencies and embedding scale are nonpersistent buffers. This establishes runtime parameter/buffer classification, not whether the scalar coefficients were learned during original training.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Unified checkpoint conversion
sources.evidence: Copies the input embedding table directly, maps multimodal weights, projects end-of-audio/end-of-image embeddings into existing token rows, and keeps lm_head tied. The inspected conversion contains no added vocabulary padding. Assistant/drafter conversion is a separate variant.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: Freshly reread the complete July 2 first-party report on October 27. Table 1 gives the 12B row 1,000M embedder, 10,890M einsums and a separate 400M drafter; only the starred 26B-A4B row labels an active einsum count. Section 2.3 states 12B was trained from scratch with new unified vision/audio projections. Section 2.5 explains per-block scalar scales for fp16 stability without their training provenance. The report gives no separately defined 12B active total; neither the einsum subtotal nor another variant’s active count applies.

sources.title: Official Gemma 4 12B IT assistant model card
sources.evidence: The separately published assistant repository is explicitly an MTP draft model that extends the main model for speculative decoding. It is not part of the audited main IT checkpoint.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Apache License 2.0
sources.evidence: The license link from the exact IT card resolves to the Apache License 2.0 text.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 JAX Transformer block
sources.evidence: The shared Gemma 4 Block creates skip_scale with self.param and multiplies block output by it. The inspected code does not specify original optimization history. The Unified converter maps skip_scale to layer_scalar, conflicting with Transformers buffer classification as a basis for an exact learned-parameter count.

sources.title: Google JAX released Gemma 4 configurations
sources.evidence: This inspected revision defines E2B, E4B, 31B and 26B A4B classes, but no 12B Unified class. Its shared-block parameter convention is supporting family evidence, not direct proof of exact Unified training provenance.

sources.title: Official named Gemma 4 12B base-model card
sources.evidence: Freshly read the complete raw base-model card on October 27, following the exact IT card’s base_model metadata. It repeats the dense 12B Unified total of 11.95B. Its 3.8B active count belongs only to 26B A4B. The explicit IT/base relationship supports the nominal total but supplies no missing active count; 31B architecture similarity is not unchanged-weight lineage.

sources.title: Current official Gemma 4 model card
sources.evidence: Fresh current card retrieved October 27. The dense-model table gives 11.95B total for 12B Unified; its separate MoE table gives 3.8B active for 26B A4B. The benchmark table identifies 12B Unified but has no activated-parameter column or row.

sources.title: A Visual Guide to Gemma 4 12B
sources.evidence: Opened the original visual guide linked directly by Google’s June 3 developer guide, and its republished text at gemma.ai/tutorials/visual-guides/gemma-4-12b/. The original author identifies his DeepMind affiliation and credits feedback from the developer-guide authors. Describes the approximately 35M vision embedder, including roughly 26M projection plus positional lookup tables, and direct audio projection. It does not disclose an active 12B total; component sizes are not a complete per-token count. This provenance rests on Google’s direct link and original authorship, not the mirror’s branding alone.

sources.title: Gemma 4 12B IT hardware calculator
sources.evidence: Freshly opened exact-model lead claiming 12B activated. Its own methodology explicitly sets active_params_b=11.96 equal to safetensors.total because the model is dense. This is a calculator convention based on total storage, not an independent primary active-parameter disclosure. Rejected as support for the active field.

sources.title: Gemma 4 12B architecture visualizer
sources.evidence: Freshly opened exact-model lead. Lists 12.0B total, but its runs-per-token estimate is 10.8B from 2.3B attention plus 8.5B feed-forward, leaving 1.0B embeddings and 195M unaccounted. Its FAQ instead asserts every parameter is used because dense. Neither statement is sourced to a separately published primary active-count convention; the partial subtotal is not adopted.

sources.title: Gemmaclaw agent benchmark results
sources.evidence: Freshly retrieved the full original application-benchmark page on October 27 after the browser extractor rejected its size. The exact Q4_K_M 12B-IT run is identified, but the 12B-active claim occurs in size-class prose justified by dense architecture. The published result cards label only Parameters, architecture, quantization and task outcomes; there is no model-research comparison table or plot declaring an active-count convention. Its own agent-task results are primary measurements, but its unsupported all-weights-per-token assertion is not accepted as a Google specification.

name.note: The repository is the instruction-tuned 12B Unified checkpoint, distinct from its base and assistant models.

developer.note: Published by Google; the model card credits Google DeepMind.

family.note: Gemma 4 belongs to the Gemma family.

release_date.note: The official release log and dated developer announcement agree on June 3, 2026.

open_weights.note: Official model weights are public; the configuration and checkpoint header were accessible without authentication.

license.note: The exact repository and its linked license specify Apache 2.0.

parameters_b.note: Rounded complete main-checkpoint parameter estimate, in billions. Header total is 11,959,730,224 BF16 elements; applying Transformers parameter/buffer convention removes 48 layer scalars, yielding 11,959,730,176. Both round to 11.9597B. Google JAX represents corresponding skip_scale values with self.param, while the report explains their fp16 stabilization role without establishing training provenance, so no exact learned count is asserted. Includes text and all vision/audio embedders/projections, counts tied embedding/output once, and excludes the separate MTP assistant. No conversion-added vocabulary padding found. The model card’s 11.95B and name’s 12B are nominal. October 27 re-audit freshly confirms the official nominal 11.95B total and explicit 12B base-to-IT lineage. The existing supported rounded total is retained; no tensor census was repeated.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model total, active, activated, component and named-base searches included later primary comparison tables and arXiv, NVIDIA, Microsoft and Qwen research domains. Reopened the pinned IT card/configuration, named base card, current Google card, launch developer guide, complete July technical report and Google-linked visual guide. None establishes a separate 12B active count: Google labels only the 26B-A4B variant active; the report’s 10.89B einsums, 1.0B embedder and separate 0.4B drafter are distinct components. The 12B model was trained from scratch, so 31B architectural similarity cannot transfer a count. Concrete 11.96B/12B and 10.8B web leads were checked: they copy total because dense or omit embeddings/unaccounted components, rather than supplying a supported primary nominal active-count convention. Gemmaclaw publishes original application tests but its all-12B-active prose is an architectural assumption, not a model-research active-parameter comparison. Leave null rather than relabel total or non-embedding subtotal.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only Transformer with 48 layers and alternating local/global attention; unified multimodal inputs use projections instead of separate audio/vision encoders.

context_window.note: Exact max_position_embeddings in the checkpoint config; the card uses the 256K shorthand.

modalities.note: Audio is projected from waveform frames; video is processed as sequences of image frames. Output is text.

reasoning.note: The exact card includes enable_thinking=True usage and configurable thinking tokens.

tool_call.note: The developer reports function-calling support, satisfying the source-reported capability definition.

description.value: Google’s instruction-tuned Gemma 4 model with a dense, encoder-free Transformer, text, image, audio and video inputs, text output, configurable thinking and function calling.
description.note: Replaces promotional compact/local-chat wording with verified model structure and capabilities.

patch.description: Google’s instruction-tuned Gemma 4 model with a dense, encoder-free Transformer, text, image, audio and video inputs, text output, configurable thinking and function calling.
patch.notes: Approximately 11.9597B parameters in the main checkpoint, including multimodal projections and tied embedding/output weights once; Google reports a nominal 11.95B. The separate MTP assistant is excluded. Runtime conventions differ on 48 layer scalars, without changing the rounded total. No separate active-parameter count was found in the checked primary sources. Video is processed as image frames.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit preserves the supported 11.9597B rounded main-checkpoint total and confirms Google’s nominal 11.95B through the exact IT and named base cards. Fresh original sources and later comparison searches do not establish a separate active count; secondary dense-equals-total and partial-subtotal estimates were rejected. Explicitly patch active_parameters_b to null. Existing release, license, architecture, modalities and other field assessments are unchanged. No weights or tensor census were downloaded or repeated.
